messages.content: Can you send to Mom an Email saying we should go out and play if Friday is okay.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
Sure! To help you draft the email, could you please share:

1. Your mom’s email address (or at least her email domain so I can format the address correctly).
2. Your name (so I can personalize the greeting).

Once I have those details, I’ll craft a friendly email for you.
message.reasoning: The user wants me to send an email to Mom asking if Friday is okay to go out and play. I need to ask for the email address or contact details? The user didn't provide Mom's email address. According to policy, I cannot fabricate personal data. So I should ask for Mom's email address. Also, I can ask for the user's name to personalize. The user might want me to send it. But I can't send emails directly. I can draft the email content. So I will ask for Mom's email address and maybe the user's name. Then I can produce a draft.
